knowledge_point.title: Evaluating a Partial Derivative at a Point

question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sin{(x )} \cos{(y )}-x y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\sin{(x )} \cos{(y )})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(x y) \\  & =\cos{(y )}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sin{(x )})-y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x) \\  & =\cos{(y )}\cdot (\cos{(x )})-y\cdot (1) \\  & =\cos{(x )} \cos{(y )}-y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(0,\pi):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(0,\pi) & =\cos{((0) )} \cos{((\pi) )}-(\pi) \\  & =(-1)\cdot (1)-(\pi) \\  & =- \pi - 1\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=x^{3} \ln{(y )}-2 \sqrt{x} y,$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(1,e).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{3} \ln{(y )}-2 \sqrt{x} y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{3} \ln{(y )})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 \sqrt{x} y) \\  & =\ln{(y )}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{3})-2 y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x}) \\  & =\ln{(y )}\cdot (3 x^{2})-2 y\cdot (\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}) \\  & =3 x^{2} \ln{(y )}-\frac{y}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(1,e)} & =3 (1)^{2} \ln{((e) )}-\frac{(e)}{\sqrt{(1)}} \\  & =3 - e\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=e^{x} \ln{(y )}+y x^{7},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(1,\frac{1}{2}).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e^{x} \ln{(y )}+y x^{7}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(e^{x} \ln{(y )})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(y x^{7}) \\  & =e^{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\ln{(y )})+x^{7}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y) \\  & =e^{x}\cdot (\frac{1}{y})+x^{7}\cdot (1) \\  & =\frac{e^{x}}{y}+x^{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,\frac{1}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(1,\frac{1}{2})} & =\frac{e^{(1)}}{(\frac{1}{2})}+(1)^{7} \\  & =1 + 2 \cdot e\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=4 y x^{2}-y^{4} x,$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(2,1).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 y x^{2}-y^{4} x) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(4 y x^{2})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{4} x) \\  & =4 x^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y)-x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{4}) \\  & =4 x^{2}\cdot (1)-x\cdot (4 y^{3}) \\  & =4 x^{2}-4 y^{3} x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(2,1)} & =4 (2)^{2}-4 (1)^{3} (2) \\  & =16-(8) \\  & =8\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=y^{2} \sqrt{x}+\frac{x}{y},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(4,2).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2} \sqrt{x}+\frac{x}{y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2} \sqrt{x}+x{y}^{-1}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2} \sqrt{x})+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{-1}) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y^{2})+x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{-1}) \\  & =\sqrt{x}\cdot (2 y)+x\cdot (-{y}^{-2}) \\  & =2 y \sqrt{x}-x{y}^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(4,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(4,2)} & =2 (2) \sqrt{(4)}-(4){(2)}^{-2} \\  & =8-(1) \\  & =7\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=2 x \sqrt{y}-4 \sqrt{x} y,$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(1,4).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x \sqrt{y}-4 \sqrt{x} y) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x \sqrt{y})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(4 \sqrt{x} y) \\  & =2 \sqrt{y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x)-4 y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\sqrt{x}) \\  & =2 \sqrt{y}\cdot (1)-4 y\cdot (\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}) \\  & =2 \sqrt{y}-\frac{2 y}{\sqrt{x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,4):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(1,4)} & =2 \sqrt{(4)}-\frac{2 (4)}{\sqrt{(1)}} \\  & =4-(8) \\  & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=\ln{(y )} \cos{(x )}-x \sin{(y )},$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂y}$ at the point $(\pi,\frac{\pi}{2}).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\ln{(y )} \cos{(x )}-x \sin{(y )}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\ln{(y )} \cos{(x )})-\frac{∂}{∂y}(x \sin{(y )}) \\  & =\cos{(x )}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\ln{(y )})-x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\sin{(y )}) \\  & =\cos{(x )}\cdot (\frac{1}{y})-x\cdot (\cos{(y )}) \\  & =\frac{\cos{(x )}}{y}-x \cos{(y )}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(\pi,\frac{\pi}{2}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y}{|}_{(\pi,\frac{\pi}{2})} & =\frac{\cos{((\pi) )}}{(\frac{\pi}{2})}-(\pi) \cos{((\frac{\pi}{2}) )} \\  & =- \frac{2}{\pi}+(0) \\  & =- \frac{2}{\pi}\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: For the function $f(x,y)=y \ln{(x )}-2 x^{5} \cdot e^{y},$ evaluate ${f}_{x}(1,\ln{(3 )}).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants:

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y \ln{(x )}-2 x^{5} \cdot e^{y}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y \ln{(x )})-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2 x^{5} \cdot e^{y}) \\  & =y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\ln{(x )})-2 \cdot e^{y}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{5}) \\  & =y\cdot (\frac{1}{x})-2 \cdot e^{y}\cdot (5 x^{4}) \\  & =\frac{y}{x}-10 x^{4} \cdot e^{y}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,\ln{(3 )}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(1,\ln{(3 )}) & =\frac{(\ln{(3 )})}{(1)}-10 (1)^{4} \cdot e^{(\ln{(3 )})} \\  & =\ln{(3 )}-10\cdot 3 \\  & =-30 + \ln{(3 )}\end{aligned}
$$
